title: Northstar Motors — 18 practical assignments
status: Training assignment specifications. Completed solutions and learner execution results are not included.
submission: Choose an assignment, implement it in a training org, and submit the permitted files or a PR URL through the portal. Include a change explanation and actual verification results. Email and optional Skool information belong in the portal profile, not public evidence. GitHub issues are an optional fallback.

assignments.title: Data model for test-drive bookings
assignments.brief: Extend the core Vehicle and Test Drive schema for Northstar Motors. Preserve the lookup relationship and independent appointment ownership; explain each new field in business terms.
prerequisites: Objects, fields, records, and lookup relationships.
The core starter is deployed in a training org.
tasks: Inspect the starter fields before adding anything.
Add Duration_Minutes__c as a whole-number field and enforce a permitted range of 15–120 minutes.
Require Vehicle__c, Customer__c, and Scheduled_At__c when Status__c is Confirmed; Requested records may remain incomplete.
Create a usable record page and synthetic examples, then retrieve only the changed metadata.
acceptance: Valid appointments save; invalid inputs produce useful messages.
15 and 120 are accepted; 0 and 121 are rejected.
The Vehicle relationship remains a lookup with independent Test Drive ownership.
The submission includes only relevant changed metadata.
failureCases: Confirm without a customer.
Test values at and outside the duration boundaries.
Delete a linked synthetic vehicle and explain the cleared optional lookup.
deliverables: Fields, validation rules, and relevant page metadata.
A table of at least six expected and actual scenarios.
A short explanation of the lookup choice.
reviewQuestions: How would master-detail change ownership and access?
Why is a page-layout requirement different from a validation rule?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record your metadata/Apex version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Salesperson and manager permissions
assignments.brief: Anna and Max need their own appointments; Oleg needs the defined team view. Configure minimal object, field, and record access without broad View All or Modify All grants.
prerequisites: Object permissions, field-level security, ownership, and private defaults.
Synthetic vehicles, Contacts, and Test Drive records.
tasks: Write a matrix separating CRUD, FLS, and record access for each persona.
Create a small permission set that does not allow VIN editing.
Choose a deliberate sharing mechanism for the required records.
Verify three personas, using sequential restricted-user experiments if the org lacks simultaneous licenses.
Identify the source of every allowed operation.
acceptance: Evidence comes from restricted personas rather than only an administrator.
Record sharing is not described as object Read.
Hiding a field in a layout is not presented as FLS.
Live and sequential persona tests are labeled accurately.
failureCases: Object Read exists but the required record is hidden.
A record is shared but object Read is missing.
A field is hidden only in the page layout.
deliverables: Relevant permission and sharing metadata.
An access matrix with at least six checks.
The smallest correction for one observed access failure.
reviewQuestions: Why can sharing fail to make a record readable?
Which independent paths could explain unexpected access?
assignments.environment: Separate training org with synthetic data and the core starter. User licenses and editions can limit simultaneous persona tests; document the actual method. Baseline API 68.0.

assignments.title: Record-triggered Flow for a single reminder
assignments.brief: The first confirmation of a Northstar test drive creates one follow-up Task. Later edits and repeated status transitions must not create another reminder for the same defined operation.
prerequisites: Record-triggered Flow, decisions, and prior values.
The difference between a Task and a Test Drive record.
tasks: Define the first-confirmation transition and what counts as the same reminder.
Create the Flow and choose a Task owner; include the Test Drive number in the subject.
If linking the customer, use the Contact as WhoId. Do not assume Activities are enabled for Test_Drive__c; the starter disables them.
Prevent duplicates after harmless edits and Confirmed→Requested→Confirmed.
Record completion only after the reminder is actually created and handle the error path visibly.
acceptance: The first confirmation creates one Task.
Repeated saves and the defined status cycle leave one Task.
A ten-record operation produces one reminder per intended appointment.
An error cannot leave a false success marker.
failureCases: Insert a record already Confirmed.
Repeat the status cycle.
Cause a controlled owner or validation failure in the training org.
deliverables: Flow and any explicitly added support fields.
Expected/actual results for at least five scenarios.
A short sanitized demonstration.
reviewQuestions: Why is checking only the current Confirmed status insufficient?
What state should remain when Task creation fails?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Bulk Apex for overdue appointments
assignments.brief: Implement TestDriveStatusService to cancel only Requested or Confirmed appointments strictly before a supplied cutoff. Completed, Cancelled, and future appointments remain unchanged.
prerequisites: Apex collections, SOQL, DML, and assertions.
The existing Test Drive status and scheduled-time fields.
tasks: Accept a set of record IDs and an explicit Datetime cutoff.
Define empty input, unknown IDs, and null scheduled-time behavior.
Keep queries and DML out of record-by-record loops.
Create TestDriveStatusServiceTest for zero, one, boundary, and 200 mixed records.
State the class API version and intended security mode.
acceptance: One and 200 records produce correct results.
The equality boundary is preserved: an appointment exactly at the cutoff is not overdue.
Repeated processing is safe.
A deliberate change to the rule causes a relevant assertion to fail.
failureCases: Empty input.
Scheduled time exactly equals the cutoff.
Mixed statuses and dates in one call.
A restricted user lacks required access.
deliverables: Apex classes, metadata, and actual test results.
An explanation of query/DML usage and protected records.
Evidence of the controlled mutation failure and restored passing result.
reviewQuestions: Why is coverage alone insufficient?
What must change or remain true when a trigger calls this service?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: LWC appointment list and interface states
assignments.brief: Create a Test Drive list that makes loading, empty results, successful data, and errors understandable to a user.
prerequisites: JavaScript basics and an LWC template/controller.
Authorized access to synthetic Test Drive records.
tasks: Choose a standard data mechanism or justify an Apex read.
Display appointment number, date, status, and safe record navigation without exposing unnecessary fields.
Implement loading, empty, success, and error states with a read-only Retry action.
Make controls keyboard-operable and provide clear labels.
Verify that the interface respects the intended user's access.
acceptance: All four states can be reproduced.
A failed read can be retried without a full page reload.
Labels and visible keyboard focus support operation.
A user is not shown data merely because the administrator can see it.
failureCases: No matching records.
An API or permission error.
Rapid repeated Retry actions.
Long text and a narrow viewport.
deliverables: LWC and required metadata.
A demonstration of the four states.
A short explanation of the LDS, UI API, or Apex choice.
reviewQuestions: Why must loading end on both success and failure?
Which state belongs only to the component and which is persisted in the org?

assignments.title: Preparing a solution for review
assignments.brief: Choose J-L01–J-L05 and make the work reproducible for another developer through portal files or a PR in your personal repository.
prerequisites: One implemented Junior assignment.
Basic Git diff and the submission guide.
tasks: Collect only changed metadata and declared dependencies.
Write a README with the requirement, API/org type, deployment steps, synthetic data, and verification steps.
Submit a focused PR URL or the portal's permitted files with clear labels.
Attach actual test evidence and explicitly list checks that were not run.
Perform a self-review and correct one concrete issue before requesting review.
acceptance: A reviewer can understand the change in two minutes and reproduce the verification.
No auth files, real customer data, or full-org dump is included.
Static checks and real org tests are distinguished.
The assignment ID and evidence refer to the current solution version.
failureCases: A required field or permission dependency is omitted.
Instructions assume the wrong working directory.
A screenshot describes an older version.
deliverables: A focused PR or permitted file package.
README and submission metadata.
Matching source and test evidence.
reviewQuestions: What makes a result reproducible?
When should a large change be split into separate PRs?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Permission Set Groups and muting
assignments.brief: A coordinator can still edit VIN after that permission was muted in one group. Find independent grants and prove the effective permission model.
prerequisites: J-L02 access layers.
Permission Sets and Permission Set Groups.
tasks: Create a VIN-edit permission set and include it in Sales Coordinator and Data Steward groups; mute VIN Edit only in the coordinator group.
Test coordinator only, coordinator plus direct permission set, both groups, and coordinator after independent grants are removed.
Wait for current group recalculation before drawing conclusions.
Keep a source→group contribution→effective permission table and distinguish Read, Edit, object access, and record access.
Choose the smallest correction without breaking the Data Steward requirement.
acceptance: A clean coordinator persona reads but does not edit VIN.
Direct and other-group grants are accounted for independently.
Muting is not described as a global user deny.
Restricted-user results and group calculation state are recorded.
failureCases: The profile or another permission set grants Edit.
The group has not finished recalculating.
The layout hides a field while API access remains.
deliverables: Permission set, group, and muting metadata.
Four-configuration expected/actual matrix.
A small contribution diagram and justified correction.
reviewQuestions: Why does muting not cancel a direct assignment?
How do you distinguish field Edit from record Edit?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Apex managed sharing when the manager changes
assignments.brief: Maintain Read access for the user in Project__c.Manager__c while preserving every independent reason for access.
prerequisites: J-L04 bulk Apex.
Private defaults, share objects, RowCause, and CRUD/FLS.
tasks: Create Project__c with private sharing, Text Name, and Manager__c lookup to User; optionally link a Vehicle. Define who may assign managers.
Add a custom Apex Sharing Reason for this business grant.
Handle insert, A→B, A→empty, and empty→A; define inactive-manager and manager-as-owner behavior.
Handle delete/undelete and owner changes according to an explicit lifecycle.
Change only shares with your own RowCause. Preserve Manual, Owner, and other processes' reasons.
Test 200 records, repeated processing, and the authorized entry point. Record API version and privileged-operation mode.
acceptance: The current manager obtains the intended Read when object permissions allow it.
The old owned grant is removed; independent access may legitimately remain.
Processing does not create duplicates or use SOQL/DML per record.
Tests cover clearing, owner changes, restoration, and preservation of another reason.
Ordinary callers cannot grant arbitrary access through an exposed service.
failureCases: A→B while A has a separate Manual share.
Manager equals owner; redundant shares need not exist if access is proven.
Delete and restore a project.
One invalid manager among 200 inputs under the declared failure policy.
deliverables: Project schema, sharing reason, Apex, and tests.
At least eight lifecycle transitions with expected results.
Own-RowCause evidence and an explanation of the privilege boundary.
reviewQuestions: Why not delete every share for the previous manager?
How does changing Manager differ from changing Owner?
What should the bulk test prove beyond no exception?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Queueable warranty checks with HTTP mocks
assignments.brief: A salesperson requests a warranty check and sees its result later. Use a fictional contract and HttpCalloutMock; no real provider is required.
prerequisites: Queueable Apex and Database.AllowsCallouts.
Test.setMock, HTTP, and JSON.
tasks: Declare Warranty_Request__c with Vehicle lookup, unique request key, status, result, attempt count, and safe error fields.
Define transitions from Queued through Processing to Succeeded or Failed, and distinguish a business-negative response from transport failure.
Specify GET /warranty/{vin}: 200 with covered and expiresOn, 404 not found, 429/5xx temporary failures, plus timeout and malformed JSON.
Enqueue work and expose request state. Reusing the same key must not create a second business request.
Use Named Credentials for any optional live endpoint; mandatory tests use mocks and no secrets.
Assert outgoing method/VIN and each outcome; identify the worker's permissions.
acceptance: Tests make no real network requests and assert final data.
200, 404, 429, 500, timeout, and invalid JSON are distinguishable.
A repeated key does not create a duplicate result.
Failed work does not remain indefinitely Processing; bounded manual retry is described.
Logs do not expose tokens or unrestricted payloads.
failureCases: 200 without required covered.
Repeat an already completed request.
Remote success followed by local persistence failure; document the current limitation.
deliverables: Apex, mock fixtures, tests, and declared metadata.
API contract and state diagram.
Actual test evidence with optional live-call evidence separately labeled.
reviewQuestions: Why are 404 and timeout different?
Does one Queueable guarantee one external business effect?
What does a mock test leave unverified?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Batch Apex with partial failures and reruns
assignments.brief: Cancel overdue unconfirmed appointments in bounded transactions and make every success, skipped record, and failure visible.
prerequisites: J-L04 cancellation rule.
Batch start/execute/finish and partial DML results.
tasks: Fix one cutoff for the entire run and select only eligible statuses before that time.
Choose a scope using SOQL, DML, CPU, and heap work per transaction.
Record success/error counts, run identity, and safe reasons; justify Database.Stateful and distinguish instance from static state.
Retry only failed work and preserve idempotent behavior for already processed records.
Keep each Apex batch unit test within one execute scope. Separately run 401 synthetic records with scope 200 as multi-scope integration evidence.
Remove synthetic data and any schedule created for the experiment.
acceptance: All intended records are accounted for without assuming execute order.
Partial errors are visible and successful work is preserved according to policy.
Completed and future appointments remain unchanged on rerun.
Unit tests do not claim several execute chunks in one test method.
Apex Jobs can be correlated with the business report.
failureCases: One validation rejection among valid inputs.
No eligible records.
Rerun after partial success.
An appointment exactly at the cutoff.
deliverables: Batch, tests, and any declared reporting schema.
Unit results and separate 401/200 run evidence.
Explanation of retained state, error policy, and rerun.
reviewQuestions: Which values survive between execute transactions?
Why does finish not prove every row succeeded?
How do you verify multiple chunks without misrepresenting a unit test?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: LWC refresh and cross-component messages
assignments.brief: Keep a Test Drive list, selected detail card, and independent indicator consistent after a successful change without reloading the page.
prerequisites: J-L05 interface states.
@api, @wire, imperative Apex, DOM events, and LMS.
tasks: Use public input and a DOM event between parent and child.
Add an independent indicator using a declared Lightning Message Channel with a minimal recordId/change-type payload.
Identify each component's source: LDS, wired Apex, or imperative Apex; refresh that actual source.
Distinguish failed saving from successful saving followed by failed refresh.
Handle rapid A→B selection with a late A response, repeated attachment, and duplicate messages.
Use Jest or a reproducible manual protocol and state which was performed.
acceptance: List, detail, and indicator converge without full reload.
Apex wire and LDS use the appropriate refresh/notification mechanisms.
A late response cannot replace the currently selected record.
Reopening does not duplicate subscriptions or actions.
After a successful save and failed refresh, the user retries only reading.
failureCases: Save succeeds but refresh fails.
Rapid selection changes.
The same message arrives twice.
The selected record becomes inaccessible.
deliverables: LWC, channel metadata, and any Apex.
A diagram of data sources, DOM boundaries, and refresh responsibilities.
Expected/actual checks for at least five states.
reviewQuestions: Why is refreshApex not universal for imperative results?
When is a DOM event simpler than LMS?
How does notifyRecordUpdateAvailable differ from a business event?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Platform Events, repeated delivery, and transactions
assignments.brief: A subscriber creates one internal result after test-drive confirmation, even if the same business event is delivered again.
prerequisites: Apex transactions and Platform Events.
Durable keys and async tests.
tasks: Create Test_Drive_Confirmed__e with Test_Drive_Id__c Text(18) and Business_Key__c Text(100); exclude unnecessary customer data.
Choose Publish After Commit for the committed confirmation and explain the alternative Publish Immediately timeline.
Persist deduplication identity consistently with the subscriber's result; account for republishing under a new event identity.
Test one repeated key, two distinct keys, and failure before completion.
Treat publish success as queue acceptance, not delivery proof. Document subscriber monitoring and recovery.
Record subscriber identity, permissions, and org constraints.
acceptance: Repeated business identity produces one result while distinct events remain processable.
No handled marker exists without the intended result.
Publisher, event bus, and subscriber transactions are distinct in the diagram.
Event test API evidence is not described as live external replay.
No exactly-once delivery guarantee is claimed.
failureCases: Same business key with different EventUuid values.
Subscriber failure before completion.
Deleted or inaccessible referenced record.
Changed event order; state the supported policy or limitation.
deliverables: Event metadata, subscriber, deduplication schema, and tests.
Transaction diagram and repeat-delivery protocol.
Operator instructions for detecting and recovering a failure.
reviewQuestions: Why is EventBus.publish success insufficient?
When is EventUuid useful and when is a business key needed?
What happens if the producer rolls back?
assignments.environment: Separate Developer Edition or training org with starter/salesforce. Use synthetic data. Record the Apex/metadata version; the starter baseline is API 68.0.

assignments.title: Diagnosing list performance
assignments.brief: A Northstar appointment list is slow. Identify a measurable bottleneck and prove an improvement under comparable conditions.
prerequisites: LWC data sources and SOQL.
Query Plan, selectivity, governor limits, and measurement.
tasks: Define the user operation and separate browser rendering, network, Apex, and SOQL time.
Prepare three reproducible synthetic datasets within your org's limits; record counts, date/status/owner distribution, and payload size.
Measure several baseline runs, relevant Query Plans, returned rows, and cache conditions.
Compare at least two candidate changes, then implement one supported by the evidence.
Repeat under the same conditions and preserve access checks and stable pagination.
State the evidence limit: small-org results do not establish million-record production performance; design the unavailable load test without inventing numbers.
acceptance: Hypothesis, baseline, change, and comparable follow-up measurements are present.
Security and records are not silently removed to claim speed.
Real measurements are distinguished from projections.
Selectivity is explained using distribution, not only the existence of an index.
Pagination covers tied timestamps, the last page, and filter changes.
failureCases: A filter returns most records.
A formerly rare value becomes common.
Records are added between pages.
The administrator sees more records than the salesperson.
deliverables: A focused improvement diff.
Measurement table with conditions and sanitized Query Plan.
Conclusion stating what is proven and what still needs measurement.
reviewQuestions: Why does an index not guarantee speed?
How do you distinguish query delay from rendering cost?
What regression can an unexplained LIMIT 100 hide?

assignments.title: Concurrent booking and record locking
assignments.brief: Two salespeople confirm overlapping appointments for one vehicle. Prevent conflicting success and explain the transaction and retry policy.
prerequisites: Transactions, record locking, and FOR UPDATE.
Bulk Apex, async work, and concurrency basics.
tasks: Define the invariant: one vehicle cannot have overlapping Confirmed appointments. Add Duration_Minutes__c if it does not exist.
Draw interleavings where both users read availability before writing and where workers acquire several records in opposite order.
Implement the chosen serialization/locking boundary and recheck eligibility within it.
Use bounded retry or a clear refusal; do not loop indefinitely.
Run unit cases and a small parallel experiment. If a second client is unavailable, submit an explicit interleaving model labeled as not live concurrency evidence.
Explain contention around a popular vehicle, shared owner, or lookup and propose measurements before redesigning.
acceptance: Two successful overlapping confirmations are not an accepted result.
Availability checking and saving are coordinated transactionally.
Failure does not leave partially confirmed records.
The report states whether concurrency was actually reproduced.
Retry limits and exhaustion behavior are visible.
failureCases: Two users confirm the same vehicle/time.
Intervals touch at a boundary; define whether that is allowed.
Two operations acquire multiple vehicles in opposite order.
The user repeats Confirm after a timeout.
deliverables: Apex, metadata, and unit tests.
Two interleaving diagrams and the invariant.
Live parallel evidence or a clearly labeled model with a follow-up test plan.
reviewQuestions: Why is checking Available before DML insufficient?
Which related records can also be locked?
How can retry increase overload?

assignments.title: Access-model migration and deferred sharing
assignments.brief: Plan a regional access reorganization and explain visibility before, during, and after sharing recalculation.
prerequisites: Managed sharing and independent access sources.
Roles, groups, sharing rules, and migration planning.
tasks: Create a small two-region model with salespeople and managers; define before/after access matrices.
Map group-membership calculations, sharing-rule calculations, and independent grants.
Write a runbook covering feature/permission checks, baseline, change window, appropriate suspension, changes, resume, required recalculation, completion monitoring, and access verification.
Explain stale-access risk during the window and changes not covered by deferral.
Define stop/go criteria, ownership, monitoring, and recovery; distinguish metadata rollback from calculated sharing state.
Perform live deferral only in a dedicated entitled training org. The mandatory basic-org result is the model and runbook.
acceptance: At least eight positive and negative before/after checks are specified.
The procedure does not stop at Resume; recalculation requirements and completion are verified.
Actual edition/feature availability and exercise mode are stated.
Deferral is not described as an access grant or immediate revocation.
Old excessive access is checked as well as new required access.
failureCases: The process stops after group changes.
Resume occurs without confirmed final recalculation.
A separate role or manual share still grants access.
Users work during a window with stale access.
deliverables: Runbook with checkpoints and recovery.
Dependency diagram and access matrix.
Small-model evidence and a list of operations not run.
reviewQuestions: Which calculations are deferred?
Why does successful metadata deployment not prove final access?
How will you find excessive access after migration?
assignments.environment: Separate training org and synthetic data. Defer Sharing Calculation depends on feature availability and permissions. The required basic-org result is a reproducible model and operational plan; live deferral is optional. Record API version; starter baseline 68.0.

assignments.title: Recovering an integration after an outage
assignments.brief: Extend the warranty integration for a two-hour provider outage, uncertain remote outcomes, and safe backlog recovery.
prerequisites: M-L03 mock integration.
Idempotency, retry, correlation, and async limits.
tasks: Extend the fictional provider contract with an idempotent create operation and status lookup; do not attribute these capabilities to an unverified real provider.
Define states including UnknownOutcome and distinguish business rejection, transient failure, and uncertain completion.
Implement bounded backoff with an upper limit and optional jitter using a controllable clock in tests.
Reconcile requests whose remote result may exist while the local result is missing.
Mock two failures then success, remote success with local timeout, repeated input, and permanent business rejection.
Create an operator view/report for queue age, attempts, reasons, safe retry, and stopping intake; estimate backlog recovery capacity.
acceptance: One business key does not create repeated external effects under the declared mock contract.
Retry exhaustion remains observable.
An unknown outcome is not mislabeled as definite success or failure.
Tests require neither a server nor two hours of waiting.
External idempotency is an explicit contract requirement, with limitations stated when absent.
failureCases: Timeout after remote persistence.
Permanent 400 versus transient 503.
Input grows faster than processing.
An operator retries twice while an older attempt finishes late.
deliverables: Extended implementation, mocks, and tests.
State diagram, capacity estimate, and retry policy.
Incident and backlog-recovery runbook.
reviewQuestions: Why is exactly-once too strong a blanket promise?
How does reconciliation differ from retry?
When should intake stop instead of retries accelerating?

assignments.title: Security review of an application path
assignments.brief: Review a complete button-to-database path and prove the relevant access boundaries under restricted users.
prerequisites: M-L01/M-L02 permission and sharing models.
Apex API versions/access modes, LWC, CRUD/FLS, and response data.
tasks: Choose a service and list its entry points, running identities, class API versions, sharing contexts, database modes, and returned fields.
Use current documentation: API 67+ defaults differ from older versions. Make critical modes explicit.
Test a user with object access but no record, a user with record access but no field, and Read without Edit.
Create one controlled local defect, such as an excessive DTO field or an unguarded privileged entry point; fix it with a test that failed beforehand.
If using restriction rules, state supported object/edition and context; do not assume a universal system-context deny.
Inspect user messages, logs, and browser responses using synthetic data only.
acceptance: Sharing, CRUD, FLS, and business rules remain distinct.
Evidence uses restricted personas.
No broad permission is added merely to bypass failure.
The regression test detects the original defect.
Unverified boundaries are listed explicitly.
failureCases: Direct Apex invocation with another user's record ID.
A hidden UI field appears in the response.
Permission is revoked after page load.
API 66 and 68 code is compared without accounting for defaults.
deliverables: Security map for one complete path.
Correction diff and positive/negative tests.
A small threat model and remaining limitations.
reviewQuestions: What does with sharing guarantee, and what requires separate analysis?
Why is API version part of a security review?
When is privileged execution justified and how is its entry constrained?

How does a training demo differ from production readiness?

sources.title: Set an Access Mode for Database Operations
